chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid from Abu Al-Hasan the Second (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'We have been narrated in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would clean himself (with stones/water) and his ring was on his finger, and similarly the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did that. And the engraving of the ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was: Muhammad (peace be upon him) the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'They spoke the truth.' I said, 'So should we do it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, those people were wearing their rings on the right hand, and indeed you are wearing your rings on the left hand.'

He (the narrator) said, 'So I was silent, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what was the engraving of the ring of Adam (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'No.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' And the engraving of the ring of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was: Muhammad the Messenger of Allah; and the ring of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was: Allah the King; and the ring of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was: The Honour is for Allah; and the ring of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was: Indeed Allah will fulfill His command; and Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) [wore] the ring of his father; and Abu Ja'far al-Akbar [wore] the ring of his grandfather Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); and the ring of Ja'far (peace be upon him) was: Allah is my Guardian and my protection from His creation; and Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) [wore]: Allah is Sufficient for me; and Abu Al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him) [wore]: Whatever Allah willed, there is no strength except with Allah.'
And Al-Husayn ibn Khalid said, 'And he extended his hand to me and said: 'My ring is also the ring of my father (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.خَاتَم: Ring (used for sealing documents or as jewelry)
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: To clean oneself (after relieving oneself) using stones or water

ai.seo_question: What were the inscriptions on the rings of the Prophet and the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the evolution of the custom of wearing rings, noting the transition from the right hand (as practiced by the Prophet and early Imams) to the left hand in later traditions, while affirming the spiritual significance of the inscriptions. It provides a detailed genealogy of the specific divine names and phrases engraved on the rings of the Twelve Imams, linking their authority directly to the Prophet's legacy. This serves as both a practical guideline for ritual purity practices and a theological affirmation of the Imams' unique status.
